test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 16th November 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: After giving a discount of 20% on the marked price of an article, it is sold for Rs. 120. Had the discount not been given, the profit would have been 20%. What is the cost price of the article?
solution:
Given:

After giving a discount of 20% on MP, SP = Rs. 120

If the discount has not been given, Profit = 20%.

Concept used:

SP = MP - MP × Discount %

SP = CP + CP × Gain%

Calculation:

Let, MP of the article = Q, and CP of the article = P

According to the question,

⇒ Q - Q × 20% = 120

⇒ Q - 0.2Q = 120

⇒ 0.8Q = 120

⇒ Q = 120/0.8

⇒ Q = 150

Now,

⇒ P + P × 20% = 150

⇒ P + 0.2P = 150

⇒ 1.2P = 150

⇒ P = 150/1.2

⇒ P = 125

∴ The cost price of the article is Rs. 125. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Let, original MP = X

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/61723ee50cb80925821208b87b1664955ac327ee0ceb2dd1079b68b87555d2bf.png] 

X = 100 × 120/80 = 150

Let, original CP = Y

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/73e78f079224f206c7561be52c0377fa66ab110a158f17053da0458d37f4e8bd.png] 

So, Y = 100 × 150/120 = Rs. 125

∴ The cost price of the article is Rs. 125.
